# RQ1 — Differential expression

### Which genes are differentially expressed between patients with complete response and patients with progressive disease following anti-PD-L1 treatment?

Suggested tasks:

-   Prepare and explore the gene-expression data, including appropriate filtering and normalization.

-   Perform differential expression analysis between responders/non-responder using DESeq2, and identify significantly differentially expressed genes

-   Visualize the results using e.g. volcano plots and heatmaps of selected genes.

-   Investigate the biological functions of differentially expressed genes and discuss their potential relevance to immunotherapy response.

-   Discuss the limitations of the analysis, including potential confounding factors and why differential expression does not necessarily imply a causal role in treatment response.

## 1. Data preparation

### Load packages and data

```{r}
#| label: setup

# Load order matters: tidyverse (dplyr) is loaded last so that dplyr::select,
# filter and slice are not masked by AnnotationDbi / IRanges / BiocGenerics.
library(DESeq2)
library(fgsea)
library(msigdbr)
library(data.table)
library(pheatmap)
library(ggrepel)
library(tidyverse)

# Significance threshold used throughout the document
padj_cut <- 0.05

# Set group colorscheme
group_colours <- c(NR = "#D9534F", R = "#2E86C1")

# Helper: "GOBP_CELL_MIGRATION" -> "Cell migration" (optionally wrapped)
clean_label <- function(x, width = NULL) {
  x <- x |>
    str_remove("^GOBP_") |>
    str_replace_all("_", " ") |>
    str_to_sentence()
  if (is.null(width)) x else str_wrap(x, width = width)
}

# Load datasets
counts   <- readRDS("../data/counts.rds")
clinical <- readRDS("../data/clinical.rds")
```

### Check that samples match

```{r}
# Samples must be identical and in the same order in both datasets
stopifnot(identical(colnames(counts), clinical$sample_id))

clinical <- as.data.frame(clinical)
rownames(clinical) <- clinical$sample_id
stopifnot(identical(colnames(counts), rownames(clinical)))

dim(counts)             # genes x samples
head(rownames(counts))  # gene names
```

All samples are present in both datasets and in the same order, so no filtering of samples is needed.

### Response as a two-level factor

```{r}
# NR is the reference level, so a positive log2 fold change
# (and a positive NES later on) means "higher in responders (R)".
clinical$BOR <- factor(clinical$BOR, levels = c("NR", "R"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(clinical$BOR))   # fails if BOR contained any other category

table(clinical$BOR)
```

## 2. Differential expression with DESeq2

### Build the DESeq2 dataset and filter low-count genes

```{r}
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts,
                              colData   = clinical,  # sample metadata
                              design    = ~ BOR)     # R vs NR

n_genes_before <- nrow(dds)

# Keep genes with at least 10 reads in total across all samples
dds <- dds[rowSums(counts(dds)) >= 10, ]
n_genes_after <- nrow(dds)

c(before = n_genes_before, after = n_genes_after)
```

### Run DESeq2 and extract results

DESeq2 normalizes the counts internally with the median-of-ratios method (size factors), so the raw counts are used as input.

```{r}
dds <- DESeq(dds)
resultsNames(dds)   # "BOR_R_vs_NR"

# Contrast means positive log2FC = higher in R
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("BOR", "R", "NR"), alpha = padj_cut)
summary(res)
```

```{r}
res_tbl <- as.data.frame(res) |>
  rownames_to_column("gene") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  drop_na(padj, log2FoldChange) |>
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      padj < padj_cut & log2FoldChange > 0 ~ "Up in responders",
      padj < padj_cut & log2FoldChange < 0 ~ "Up in non-responders",
      TRUE ~ "Not significant"
    )
  )

n_tested <- nrow(res_tbl)
n_up     <- sum(res_tbl$group == "Up in responders")
n_down   <- sum(res_tbl$group == "Up in non-responders")

# Top 10 genes by adjusted p-value
res_tbl |>
  filter(group != "Not significant") |>
  arrange(padj) |>
  select(gene, group, log2FoldChange, padj, baseMean) |>
  head(10)

res_tbl |>
  filter(group != "Not significant") |>
  arrange(log2FoldChange) |>
  select(gene, group, log2FoldChange, padj, baseMean) |>
  head(10)
```

Of the `{r} n_tested` genes with an adjusted p-value, `{r} n_up` were significantly higher in responders and `{r} n_down` were significantly higher in non-responders (BH-adjusted p \< `{r} padj_cut`).

#### **Interpretation**

Comment on the number of DE genes. Is it large or small given the sample size? Mention the top genes and what they do.

### Sample level overview

```{r}
# Variance-stabilising transformation for visualisation only (not used for the DE test)
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = TRUE) # could also have been log2 transformation, vst is build specifically for rna seq count data

pca <- plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = "BOR") +
  scale_color_manual(values = group_colours) +
  labs(title = "PCA of variance-stabilised counts") +
  theme_minimal()
pca

ggsave("images/pca.pdf", pca, width = 10, height = 6, device = cairo_pdf)
```

#### Interpretation

Not divided by response, not the main driver of seperation (age, sex, batch effect, TMB etc etc)

29% variance explained

### Volcano plot (top 5 numeric largest Log2FC scores for both groups)

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6

# Label the 5 genes with the highest log2FC in each direction
gene_labels <- res_tbl |>
  filter(group != "Not significant") |>
  group_by(group) |>
  slice_min(
    if_else(group == "Up in responders",
            -log2FoldChange,
            log2FoldChange),
    n = 5,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) |>
  ungroup()

deseq_volcano_log2fc <- ggplot(res_tbl, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj))) +
  geom_point(aes(color = group), alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(padj_cut), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c("Up in responders"     = group_colours[["R"]],
               "Up in non-responders" = group_colours[["NR"]],
               "Not significant"      = "grey80")
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(data = gene_labels, aes(label = gene),
                  size = 3, max.overlaps = Inf, box.padding = 0.4) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = 0, label = "Higher in responders \u2192",
           hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.5, size = 3,
           fontface = "italic", color = group_colours[["R"]]) +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = 0, label = "\u2190 Higher in non-responders",
           hjust = -0.05, vjust = -0.5, size = 3,
           fontface = "italic", color = group_colours[["NR"]]) +
  labs(x = "Log2 fold change (R vs NR)",
       y = "-Log10 adjusted p-value",
       title = "Differential expression: responders vs non-responders") +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("images/deseq_volcano_log2fc.pdf", deseq_volcano_log2fc, width = 10, height = 6, device = cairo_pdf)
```

#### Interpretation

Consider not the most significant but the most out Log2FC's

### Heatmap of the top differentially expressed genes

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7

top_genes <- res_tbl |>
  filter(group != "Not significant") |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 30, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(gene)

if (length(top_genes) >= 2) {
  mat <- assay(vsd)[top_genes, ]
  ann <- as.data.frame(colData(vsd)[, "BOR", drop = FALSE])

  pheatmap(mat,
           scale             = "row",   # z-score per gene
           annotation_col    = ann,
           annotation_colors = list(BOR = group_colours),
           color             = colorRampPalette(c(group_colours[["NR"]], "white", group_colours[["R"]]))(100),
           show_colnames     = FALSE,
           main              = "Top 30 DE genes (VST, row z-score)")
}

```

*Figure: Heatmap of the 30 most significant genes. Samples (columns) are clustered by expression and the bar at the top shows their response group.*

## 3. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA)

Gene-level tests only look at individual genes. GSEA asks whether whole biological processes are shifted towards one group, which is more robust when many genes change a little.

### Gene sets and gene ranking

```{r}
# GO Biological Process gene sets from MSigDB.
# (msigdbr >= 10 uses collection/subcollection, older versions category/subcategory)
gene_sets <- if (packageVersion("msigdbr") >= "10.0.0") {
  msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C5", subcollection = "GO:BP")
} else {
  msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "C5", subcategory = "GO:BP")
}

pathways <- split(gene_sets$gene_symbol, gene_sets$gs_name) |>
  lapply(unique)
length(pathways)

# Rank all genes by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (sign = direction, size = confidence).
# If a symbol occurs more than once, keep the row with the strongest statistic.
ranked_df <- tibble(gene = rownames(res), stat = res$stat) |>
  filter(!is.na(stat), !is.na(gene), gene != "") |>
  arrange(desc(abs(stat))) |>
  distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)

ranked_genes <- sort(setNames(ranked_df$stat, ranked_df$gene), decreasing = TRUE)

# Sanity checks on the ranked list
tibble(
  n_ranked_genes = length(ranked_genes),
  n_in_GOBP      = sum(names(ranked_genes) %in% gene_sets$gene_symbol),
  pct_ties       = 100 * mean(duplicated(ranked_genes))
)
```

### Run fgsea

```{r}
set.seed(42)   # reproducible permutations
fgsea_res <- fgseaMultilevel(pathways = pathways,
                             stats    = ranked_genes,
                             minSize  = 15,
                             maxSize  = 500)

fgsea_res <- fgsea_res[order(padj)]
fgsea_tbl <- as_tibble(fgsea_res)

n_pw_tested <- nrow(fgsea_tbl)
n_pw_sig    <- sum(fgsea_tbl$padj < padj_cut, na.rm = TRUE)

fgsea_tbl |>
  select(pathway, NES, padj, size) |>
  head(20)
```

`r n_pw_tested` GO biological processes (15-500 genes) were tested, and `r n_pw_sig` were significant (BH-adjusted p \< `r padj_cut`). A positive NES means the pathway is enriched in responders, a negative NES in non-responders.

### Top enriched pathways (before collapsing)

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9

top_pathways_df <- fgsea_tbl |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(NES > 0,
                             "Enriched in responders",
                             "Enriched in non-responders")) |>
  group_by(direction) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(label = clean_label(pathway, width = 30))

gsea_top_enriched_pathways <- ggplot(top_pathways_df, aes(x = NES, y = reorder(label, NES), fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c("Enriched in responders"     = group_colours[["R"]],
               "Enriched in non-responders" = group_colours[["NR"]])
  ) +
  labs(x = "Normalized enrichment score (NES)",
       y = NULL,
       title = "Top enriched GO biological processes",
       subtitle = "Top 5 per direction by adjusted p-value, ordered by NES") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
        legend.position    = "bottom",
        plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title.position = "plot")

ggsave("images/gsea_top_enriched_pathways.pdf", gsea_top_enriched_pathways, width = 10, height = 6, device = cairo_pdf)

gsea_top_enriched_pathways
```

GO terms overlap heavily. The next step collapses them into independent themes.

### Collapse redundant pathways

```{r}
#| warning: false
set.seed(42)

sig <- fgsea_res[padj < padj_cut][order(pval, -abs(NES))]
collapsedPathways <- collapsePathways(sig, pathways, ranked_genes, nperm = 1000)

main_pathways <- collapsedPathways$mainPathways
n_sig  <- nrow(sig)
n_main <- length(main_pathways)
```

Of the `n_sig` significant pathways, `n_main` were kept as independent main pathways. The others are largely explained by one of these main pathways.

```{r}
# Which pathways were absorbed by each main pathway?
parents  <- collapsedPathways$parentPathways
children <- tibble(pathway = names(parents), parent = parents) |>
  filter(!is.na(parent))

children |>
  group_by(parent) |>
  summarise(n_absorbed = n(),
            examples   = paste(head(pathway, 4), collapse = "; ")) |>
  arrange(desc(n_absorbed))
```

```{r}
# Statistics for the main (collapsed) pathways only
main_tbl <- fgsea_tbl |>
  filter(pathway %in% main_pathways) |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(NES > 0,
                             "Enriched in responders",
                             "Enriched in non-responders"),
         label = clean_label(pathway))

main_tbl |> 
  dplyr::count(direction)

# Top 10 main pathways per direction
main_tbl |>
  group_by(direction) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(direction, padj) |>
  select(label, direction, NES, padj, size)

fgsea_tbl |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(NES > 0,
                             "Enriched in responders",
                             "Enriched in non-responders"),
         label = clean_label(pathway)) %>% 
  group_by(direction) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(direction, padj) |>
  select(label, direction, NES, padj, size)

```

#### Interpretation

**Responders** are higher in pathways that are associated with active cell proliferation/cell division,

In the context of anti-PD-L1 treatment, this makes sense because the treatment releases the brakes on the immune system, reflecting a more proliferative tumour environment, potentially including increased immune-cell proliferation and expansion of activated lymphocytes.

However, these pathways are not specific to immune cells. They could also reflect proliferation of tumour cells. Therefore, it is important to examine which cell populations contribute to the signal.

In the article, they find that high TMB is related to treatment response, so it might be a result of this, that the reponders are high. Correlational, not causal (?)

**Non-responders** are higher in extracellular matrix remodelling which may indicate a new tumor microenvironment, as well as positive vascular development a driver of angiogenesis.

Tissue remodeling is also very much in alignment with the findings from the article

### GSEA table for the main pathways

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8

top_main_up <- main_tbl |>
  filter(NES > 0) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(pathway)

top_main_down <- main_tbl |>
  filter(NES < 0) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(pathway)


# gseaParam = 0.5 only affects how the plot is drawn, not the statistics
plotGseaTable(pathways[c(top_main_up, rev(top_main_down))],
              stats     = ranked_genes,
              fgseaRes  = main_tbl,
              gseaParam = 0.5)

```

### Enrichment plots for the top main pathway in each direction

```{r}
top_up <- main_tbl |>
  filter(NES > 0) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(pathway)

top_down <- main_tbl |>
  filter(NES < 0) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(pathway)

plot_pw <- function(pw) {
  es <- fgsea_tbl$ES[fgsea_tbl$pathway == pw]
  plotEnrichment(pathways[[pw]], ranked_genes, ticksSize = 0.08) +
    labs(title = clean_label(pw, width = 60)) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = sort(c(0, es)) + c(-0.1, 0.1))
}

# Loop + print() so that a direction without any main pathway is simply skipped
for (pw in c(top_up, top_down)) print(plot_pw(pw))
```

### Volcano plot of the collapsed pathways

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8

# Adding non-significant pathways to the plot for illustrational purposes
nes_df <- fgsea_tbl |>
  mutate(label = clean_label(pathway), 
         group = case_when(
      NES > 0 & pathway %in% main_pathways ~ "Up in responders",
      NES < 0 & pathway %in% main_pathways ~ "Up in non-responders",
      padj > padj_cut ~ "Not significant",
      TRUE ~ "Not main pathways")) %>% 
  filter(group != "Not main pathways") |> # remove significant non-main pathways
  arrange(group != "Not significant")   # draw significant points on top

# All collapsed (independent) main pathways, not only the top 10 per direction
nes_df_alternative <- main_tbl |>
  mutate(
    label = clean_label(pathway, width = 40),
    group = case_when(
      padj < padj_cut & NES > 0 ~ "Up in responders",
      padj < padj_cut & NES < 0 ~ "Up in non-responders",
      TRUE ~ "Not significant"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(group != "Not significant")   # draw significant points on top

 
# Label the 5 most significant main pathways in each direction
nes_labels <- nes_df |>
  filter(group != "Not significant") |>
  group_by(group) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

p <- ggplot(nes_df, aes(x = NES, y = -log10(padj))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(padj_cut), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_point(aes(size = size, fill = group),
             shape = 21, colour = "white", stroke = 0.35, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c("Up in responders"     = group_colours[["R"]],
               "Up in non-responders" = group_colours[["NR"]],
               "Not significant"      = "grey80"),
    aesthetics = c("color", "fill")
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Gene set size", range = c(1, 6)) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = nes_labels,
    aes(label = label, colour = group),
    size = 2.9, lineheight = 0.9, fontface = "bold",
    fill = alpha("white", 0.7), label.size = 0.25,
    label.r = unit(0.2, "lines"), label.padding = unit(0.25, "lines"),
    box.padding = 0.6, point.padding = 0.4, min.segment.length = 0,
    segment.size = 0.35, segment.curvature = -0.15, segment.ncp = 3,
    segment.inflect = TRUE, max.overlaps = Inf, seed = 42,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = 0, label = "Higher in responders \u2192",
           hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.5, size = 3,
           fontface = "italic", color = group_colours[["R"]]) +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = 0, label = "\u2190 Higher in non-responders",
           hjust = -0.05, vjust = -0.5, size = 3,
           fontface = "italic", color = group_colours[["NR"]]) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(order = 1,
                        override.aes = list(size = 4, alpha = 1)),
    size = guide_legend(order = 2,
                        override.aes = list(fill = "grey60", colour = "grey40",
                                            alpha = 0.7))
  ) +
  labs(x = "Normalized enrichment score (NES)",
       y = expression(-log[10]~"(adjusted p-value)"),
       title = "Gene-set enrichment of collapsed pathways: responders vs non-responders") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot",
        legend.position     = "top",
        plot.title          = element_text(face = "bold", size = 17))

p

dir.create("images", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave("images/gsea_volcano.pdf", p, width = 10, height = 6, device = cairo_pdf)
```

*Figure: Each point is one of the `n_main` independent (collapsed) GO biological processes. Point size shows the number of genes in the set and colour shows the direction of enrichment. All collapsed pathways were selected among the significant ones, so all points lie above the significance line.*
